title: Log-source coverage
context: At LearnTech, the partner-managed SIEM collects the logs, and threat intelligence from MISP and OpenCTI with sector ISAC feeds is matched against them. This lab's product, MISP + OpenCTI + sector ISAC feeds, is named here only for context. LogLens is a brand-neutral simulator that shows the same governance information. All log data is synthetic.
atWork: At work, a junior analyst checks the logs behind a breach notification before the DPO signs it: which sources can show what happened and when, how long that evidence is kept, and which systems that must send logs do not.
owner: INC-2610-3001's record says a release left the export link of the Learning platform & content (Amsterdam) exposed from 2026-12-07 17:30, and the platform was taken offline at 2026-12-08 14:50, both Amsterdam time (UTC+1). Your plan dates everything in UTC and says about 4,500 records were taken. Both rest on what LearnTech's security monitoring logged. Before I sign the plan, check LogLens: which of the affected system's log sources can go on the incident timeline as they are, and are their events kept long enough for the authorities' questions? The post-incident review will also ask whether every system that must send logs does: check that while you are in. Capture what you find, so I can rely on it without opening the console.
rules: Evidence is collected and preserved forensically; chain of custody maintained. … Preserve logs; note times in UTC. Start a single incident timeline.
What that means for a log source

A source's events can go on the incident timeline only if it was reporting for the whole exposure: from the moment the export link was exposed until the platform was taken offline. The DPO's note gives both, in Amsterdam time. A source whose clock offset is a minute or more goes on only with its times corrected by that offset.
Security event logs are kept for at least 12 months (365 days). The hot, searchable period may be shorter.

BKB-POL-009 Operations Security Policy, SIEM coverage, LOW value: Mission Critical + internet-facing. That is: every Mission Critical system, and every internet-facing system, sends its logs to the security monitoring platform. BKB-ADD-36 Section 8.1 lists LearnTech's Mission Critical assets.

views.title: Log sources
views.sub: Every source sending events to LogLens. System and Office are the asset register's. Source health shows how each one is doing.

views.title: Source health
views.sub: Each source's state. Status is No events when nothing has arrived for 24 hours. Clock offset is how far the source's clock is from LogLens's (+ is ahead). Connected on is when the source began sending. All times UTC.

views.title: Retention settings
views.sub: How long LogLens keeps events, per source group. Hot: searchable at once. Total: how long events are kept at all, older ones searchable after a restore.

views.title: Asset register extract
views.sub: From LearnTech's asset register, for this check: the head office's systems that serve every office, and the Amsterdam office's business systems. Connected sources counts the LogLens sources sending each system's events.

parts.title: The affected system's log sources
parts.ask: Find every log source that carries the affected system's events, and capture exactly those.
parts.where: Log sources. The DPO's note names the affected system and its office. Use two filters together. Press Capture evidence, then choose the capture here.

parts.title: Can each one go on the incident timeline?
parts.ask: For each source you captured, decide how its events can go on the incident timeline.
parts.where: Source health gives each source's Status, Last event, Clock offset and Connected on, in UTC. The DPO's note gives when the link was exposed and when the platform was taken offline, in Amsterdam time: one hour ahead of UTC in December. The rules you apply says when a source can be used.
options: Use its times as they are
Use it with its times corrected

parts.title: Are their events kept long enough?
parts.ask: For each source you captured, decide whether LogLens keeps its events as long as the Group requires.
parts.where: Log sources gives each source's Source group. Retention settings gives each group's retention. BKB-POL-009 Section 3.4 is in The rules you apply.

parts.title: Systems that send nothing
parts.ask: Find every system in the asset register extract that sends no logs to LogLens, and capture exactly those.
parts.where: Asset register extract. Connected sources counts the LogLens sources sending each system's events.

parts.title: Which of them must send logs?
parts.ask: For each system you captured, decide whether BKB-ADD-36 Section 5 requires its logs in LogLens.
parts.where: Asset register extract gives Internet-facing. BKB-ADD-36 Section 8.1 (Policies › Policy Library) lists the Mission Critical assets. Section 5's SIEM coverage line is in The rules you apply.
